summary: Boise NF L-4 ground cabin built 1933 on Dry Buck Mountain; destroyed by 1973; a climbing guide says its foundation still sits on the summit.

facts.status_note: Cabin destroyed in 1973; a climbing guide says the lookout's foundation still sits on the summit

staffing.status: stationed there in January 1945 (Idaho Statesman item quoted by Forest Lookouts); Idaho Fire Lookouts says no documented staffing history

access.note: On Boise National Forest land; the climbing guide describes road access up Forest Road 643 from Banks and mentions no closure

visit.trail_note: Per the climbing guide, the road reaches Dry Buck Summit after 11 miles; a 1.1-mile climb gaining 567 feet leads to the top. The guide does not describe current conditions.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1973; firelookout.com says gone by 1973; the climbing guide says the summit was capped until the early 1970s. Recorded as 1973 because three sources give that year; the guide's phrase is approximate.

Idaho Fire Lookouts says it has no documented staffing history, while Forest Lookouts quotes a dated January 28, 1945 Idaho Statesman item naming a person stationed at Dry Buck. The dated newspaper item is recorded; the disagreement is noted.

notes_for_editor: Site today rests on a single climbing guide (foundation still on the summit); no other source describes it. A geocaching listing (GC1D5ZQ, geocaching.com) reportedly says only a cement foundation remains, but the page could not be read in the cache, so it is not cited. Brief location conflict unchecked: FFLA 44.14623, -116.1483 vs West US Lookouts 44.12711, -116.15346. Elevation 6508 ft from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. No height_m recorded because no source gives a tower height. No usable photo URL found. Closure check: a text search of the climbing guide finds no road closure (its only match is 'Comments are closed.'). The 6508 ft elevation and Boise NF are also on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page and are now quoted as evidence.
